title: Concavity and the Second Derivative Test
subtitle: How a graph bends, where the bend changes, and a second way to sort critical numbers.

questions.text: If $f''(c) = 0$, then $c$ is an inflection point.
questions.explain: $x^4$ has $f''(0) = 0$ but is concave up on both sides. The concavity must actually **change**.
Concave down at a flat spot: max.
Concave up at a flat spot: min.

questions.text: $f'(1) = 0$ and $f''(1) = 0$. What does the second derivative test say?
options: Nothing: it fails. Use the first derivative test.

questions.text: If $f''(x) > 0$ on an interval, the graph is concave up there.
A function can be increasing and concave down at the same time.
questions.explain: Like $sqrt x$: rising, but leveling off.

questions.text: At an inflection point, $f'$ must be 0.
questions.explain: $x^3 - 3x$ has an inflection at 0, where the slope is −3.

questions.text: Here is the graph of $f''$. Where is $f$ concave up?
questions.explain: $f'' > 0$ when the line is above the axis.

questions.explain: $e^x > 0$ always, so the sign is the sign of $x + 2$.

slides.title: What the bend tells you
slides.text: Now slide along $f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 30$. The curve is **gold** where it bends up like a cup and **teal** where it bends down like a frown. Visit both.
slides.after: Concave down on the left, concave up on the right. The switch at $x$ = 2 is an **inflection point**.

slides.text: If $f''(x) > 0$, the graph is concave ___ (like a cup). If $f''(x) < 0$, it is concave ___ (like a frown).
slides.explain: The second derivative tells you which way the graph bends.
slides.hint: Positive second derivative: slopes are increasing.
